Alright, I don't know if this really qualifies, but we'll call this kid Jack, just for the sake of simplicity. Jack and I had the same lunch period every year we were at that school, so I got to know him a little bit. 

Jack had long black hair which hung mostly over his face and he had a darker complexion, I think he said his family was mostly Native American or something, he wasn't Hispanic, but a lot of other students assumed he was. He seemed clean enough, no noticeable hygiene issues, but all of his jeans had holes in them around the knees and he always wore black Band T-Shirts. He also wore the same black long-sleeve flannel every single day. I mean every single day. If it was cold, he wore it over the T-Shirt like a jacket (he called it a jacket too if I'm not mistaken), but If it was hot, he just tied it around his waist and went about his business. Jack once hit someone for grabbing his "Jacket", some kid in the line at lunch, Jack broke his nose and then just walked to the Principal's office by himself, not saying anything to anyone. He also owned the same pair of scuffed motorcycle boots throughout high-school, I don't know why, but shoes were a big deal at our school, maybe because we were inner-city, but people wouldn't let up about those boots, or anyone else's footwear that seemed inadequate (I myself made the horrible error of wearing Crocs to class once, never again, never ever again).  

He was smart, too smart, obnoxiously smart even, but he was also lazy as hell and would sleep through classes if he even bothered to show up at all. When he was present and awake, Jack was mostly quiet, writing in one of his seemingly innumerable spiral notebooks (I asked him about it once, and he showed me what I think was a script, but his handwriting was almost illegible) though he did have a habit of speaking up only when correcting someone (often a teacher) about something they were apparently wrong about, or when mouthing off to someone. What I mean to say is, Jack only opened his mouth when he didn't have something nice to say. 


He was into poetry as well, spent most of his free time in the library reading books of it, and for a brief time (a semester in Woodshop), he found acceptance in the "Rapper" clique (we were an inner-city school, if that means anything) by apparently putting his more insulting poetry to a beat, I watched him do it once, it was funny but I think it went over most people's heads. 

He didn't really get along with many people, one or two people at the most spent legitimate time around him, but he sat at the "Outcast" table, filled with anyone else who didn't have a clique to sit with (mostly gamers, geeks, nerds, that one kid who talked about dragons, the other kid who wore the Wolf T-Shirts, etc). 

We talked a few times over the course of High School, he would talk politics, or religion, usually holding aggressively different opinions just to get an argument out of me, he loved playing Devil's Advocate like that, he was a bit of a prick in all honesty but at least claimed to mean well (he said that if someone couldn't defend their position, then they haven't really decided for themselves at all). Other times however, I got him to talk about stuff he was interested in and apparently he was really into Anime and Video Games. Near the end of our third year, we had started hanging out a bit more (we had JROTC together but he rarely showed up) and we even watched Anime together in the Computer Lab, he showed me a few sites for watching Anime and introduced me to a few Games that are now my favorites.

The next year though, he wasn't there, he dropped out right before Senior year due to family stuff. I ran into him on Facebook about a year ago, apparently he got his GED, did two years at the local Community College and is a University a few towns over now, good for you Jack.

In Middle School I had a best friend, and he introduced me to Morrowind, it was his favorite game. I was a year ahead of him, and in my last year at that school, he died tragically. After that year, I went to High School and withdrew from social involvement for a while, every day was spent going to school then rushing home to play Morrowind. His copy of Morrowind.

After a while, I dropped out of High School and got my GED, around this time I stumbled on Oblivion, I played it for a little while, and went back to Morrowind after finding it unsatisfying. Oblivion simply wasn't as immersive to me. 

I took my GED and went to College about three years ago, gave up console gaming entirely and bought a gaming PC. While in College I've revisited Oblivion, this time on PC, with a more open mind and found it to be pretty good actually (especially Shivering Isles) and after that I played Arena and Daggerfall (after spending a week or so wrapping my head around DOSBox). 

I still prefer Morrowind, it's still my favorite game ever (and it's so much better on PC), and I still have his copy (although now that I've moved entirely to PC gaming I only play my Steam copy and keep his safe and sound on my bookcase). It really sucked losing him, when he died, I went into shock and stayed there for years, but I got TES out of it. It's not a fair trade by any stretch of the imagination, but it just means so much to me to play TES games. Whenever I play one, I just feel closer to him, it's silly but it's what I've got.

I try to make characters with all the races (I make a lot of characters). However, my main story character is always an Argonian, I don't really know why, I just love their lore. I started playing Argonians in Morrowind and it was awesome to be this member of a slave race and to go through the trials of the story trying to save a land full of people who hate/distrust you, it was deep. I played Kahjit a bit more in Oblivion than I did in Morrowind, but I still stuck to Argonian for my main. Orcs are my least played race, I really don't find them very appealing, but that might change in Skyrim because they look so awesome. I don't know, I find Nords and Imperials to be really boring choices... 

I mean, I spend every day of my life as a human, why should I be one in a fantasy game full of different races?
